messages.subject: exception catching in commands/samplers?
parts:
Exec summary:

I'm going to let the catch errors we're getting slide
because I don't know how to test any of my proposed fixes without
it sucking up all my time for the foreseeable future.

Various functions in the Boost math lib throw exceptions
of various kinds:

http://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_53_0/libs/math/doc/sf_and_dist/html/math_toolkit/main_overview/error_handling.html

A summary of the exception types:

Domain Error
Pole Error
Overflow Error
Underflow Error
Denormalisation Error
Rounding Error
Evaluation Error
Indeterminate Result Error

The built-in C++ exceptions are described here:

http://www.cplusplus.com/reference/exception/exception/

There are multiple blocks in the command and samplers that set up
a try/catch, but then catch

(a) domain_error only,
(b) runtime_error only, or
(c) everything.

I don't see the motivation for catching just runtime_error; it
derives from std::exception. Unfortunately, C++ exceptions can
be anything (though it's considered bad form to throw anything
other than a subclass of std::exception --- we don't do it and I
doubt Boost or Eigen do it).

I think we can do one of the following:

Option 1: just catch anything and treat it as a rejection.

Option 1a: literally catch anything (i.e., catch(...))

Option 1b: catch instances of std::exception

Option 2: list out a subset of each errors in duplicate catches

Option 1b is the simplest change and has the advantage over 1a of
allowing informative error messages.

But I don't know how to easily test the change in such a way as to
meet our stringent new every-code-change-must-be-tested policy.
I'd have to dive into mocking out just about every aspect of the commands
so that we could force exceptions of all the different types to be thrown so
that all the code could be exercised by tests. This would take me days,
if not weeks of work.

So basically, I'm blocked on this the same way I'm blocked on
doing the parser fixes. Maybe it's my own lack of imagination in
testing, but nevertheless, it's putting me off fixing this bug
that people seem to be running into (mainly from badly specified
model, but even so, we want our code to do the right thing).

We really need to review all of the command.hpp catches.
They're set up in a nesting pattern I don't understand the
motivation for (partly because the function is 700 lines long).

I would prefer to see the code factored into functions,
but then I won't get by our testing policy without testing each function.
And they're not really easy to independently test. This is an example of
where our testing policy has the negative side effect of encouraging
monolithic functions like the 700-line long command.

So for lack of ability to test, I think I'm just going to let this
error slide for now. Along with the parser fixes.

Suggestions appreciated.

I know Daniel said he'd help with testing when we got blocked, but he's
fully engaged on other projects, so it's no help for these relatively
simple, but hard to test fixes.

- Bob
